q: Which change rewrites the whole table (and so blocks it for a long time on a big table)?
options: Adding a column with a volatile default, like `DEFAULT random()`
Adding a column with a constant default
Dropping a column
Making a varchar column wider
why: A constant default, a wider varchar and a DROP COLUMN are instant. A volatile default and a type change of a different size rewrite the table.

q: Why run a migration with a short `lock_timeout`?
options: It makes the migration run faster
If it cannot get its lock quickly, it gives up instead of blocking everyone behind it. You then retry
It lets the migration skip checks
It is required by Prisma
why: It is better to fail fast than to block the site.

q: How do you add a CHECK rule to a huge live table safely?
options: Add it normally and wait
Lock the table for writes first
Add it NOT VALID (fast), then VALIDATE it later (checks old rows without blocking writes)
Copy the table and rename it
why: NOT VALID adds the rule fast. VALIDATE checks the old rows with a lock that lets writes through.

q: What is true about `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`?
options: It is always faster than a normal CREATE INDEX
It must run inside a transaction
It blocks writes, but not reads
It does not block writes, it cannot run inside BEGIN, and a failed build leaves an INVALID index to drop
why: On a live table, always use CONCURRENTLY.

q: You must fill a new column for 50 million rows. What is the safe way?
options: Update in small batches, each in its own transaction
One UPDATE for all rows in one transaction
Lock the table and run it overnight
Drop the old column first
why: Never one UPDATE for millions of rows. It holds locks long and makes a huge pile of dead rows.

q: What is the safe way to rename a column that live code uses?
options: Run ALTER TABLE RENAME and deploy at the same moment
Expand and contract: add the new column, sync, backfill, switch the code, then drop the old one last
Drop the column and add it again
Rename it during a short maintenance window only
why: Each step must work with the old code and the new code.
